newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler- German 97 GDP growth of 2.5 pct realistic.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler- German 97 GDP growth of 2.5 pct realistic.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Monday repeated that he believed Germany has a realistic chance of achieving economic growth of 2.5 percent in 1997.

"I consider growth of 2.5 percent to be achievable. What is important for me is that the export numbers are running well above expectations," he told reporters on the fringes of a Bavarian tradesmen's seminar.
Zeitler warned however that it was important to recognise that domestic investment and consumption remained weak.
"We must recognise that Germany has a Janus-headed (facing both ways) economic picture. The domestic breakthrough is not here yet."
May M3 money supply grew at an annualised rate of 7.0 percent from the final quarter of 1996, which was above market expectations. In April, M3 grew 6.7 percent.
"I still believe that we will be in the corridor this year," Zeitler said of M3 growth.
He also said the unexpectedly strong M3 growth in May was a sign of lively lending demand and weak monetary capital formation.
He said the trend might indicate a pick-up in the economy.
In the medium-term, Zeitler said Germany was very close to the Bundesbank's goals for money supply.
"I believe the European Central Bank would still do well to follow a money supply target, of course possibly accompanied by an inflation target," Zeitler said.
Zeitler also reaffirmed his belief that Germany would meet entry criteria for the single European currency without one-off measures.
"The events of recent weeks have shown that Germany can meet EMU goals without one-off measures," he said.
Asked about the agreement announced last week between the Bundesbank and the Bonn government on revaluing Bundesbank currency reserves, Zeitler said, "I consider this a good and a sensible measure."
